title: Phishing & Business Account Compromise
description: A simulated cyber incident involving a suspicious email that eventually leads to unauthorized access to a business account.

questions.story: You manage a small online business in Ghana. One morning, an employee receives an email claiming to be from a service provider the business normally uses.
questions.question: What should the employee do first?
options: Click the link immediately to check the message
Verify the message and sender before taking any action
Reply to the sender with the employee's password
questions.feedback: The safest first step is to verify the message and sender before interacting with suspicious content.

questions.story: The employee notices that the sender's address is slightly different from the address normally used by the service provider.
questions.question: What does this difference suggest?
options: The message may be impersonating a legitimate organization
The employee should send their password
questions.feedback: A suspicious sender address can be an important warning sign of impersonation or phishing.

questions.story: The email contains a link asking the employee to sign in to the business account.
questions.question: What is the safest way to verify the link?
options: Click it and enter the password
Use a known legitimate website or trusted contact to verify the request
questions.feedback: Suspicious links should be verified through a trusted channel rather than used directly.

questions.story: The employee reports that they accidentally entered their business account credentials after following the suspicious request.
questions.question: What should happen next?
options: Do nothing unless money is lost
Immediately report the suspected credential compromise
Share the credentials with another employee
questions.feedback: A suspected credential compromise should be reported immediately so protective and investigative actions can begin.

questions.story: The business receives an alert showing that the account was accessed from an unfamiliar device.
questions.question: What does this alert potentially indicate?
options: The account has been permanently deleted
questions.feedback: An unfamiliar device or login location can be an indicator of possible unauthorized access.

questions.story: The attacker appears to have accessed the business account and started sending fraudulent messages to customers.
questions.question: What should be the immediate priority?
options: Continue using the compromised account normally
Contain the incident and prevent further unauthorized activity
Delete every record related to the incident
questions.feedback: The immediate priority is containment and preventing further unauthorized activity.

questions.story: The business has contained the suspicious activity. The team now needs to understand what happened.
questions.question: What should the team preserve before investigating further?
options: Relevant incident records and available logs
questions.feedback: Relevant records and logs may be important for understanding the incident and supporting the investigation.

questions.story: The investigation begins. The team has access to simulated account login records.
evidence: 09:35 — Customer messages sent from business account
questions.question: Which record would be especially important to investigate?
questions.feedback: The unfamiliar-device login is an important forensic lead because it may indicate unauthorized access.

questions.story: The team has preserved the simulated login records and suspicious email.
questions.question: Why should the evidence be preserved carefully?
options: To maintain its reliability for investigation
To make the incident look worse
questions.feedback: Evidence should be preserved carefully so its integrity and reliability can be maintained during investigation.

questions.story: The investigator compares the timestamps from the suspicious email, login records and customer messages.
questions.question: What can timestamps help the investigator establish?
questions.feedback: Timestamps can help reconstruct the sequence and timing of events.

questions.story: The evidence shows that the suspicious email appeared before the unfamiliar login, followed by fraudulent customer messages.
questions.question: What does this sequence potentially suggest?
questions.feedback: The sequence may indicate a relationship between the phishing event, unauthorized access and subsequent activity.

questions.story: The investigation indicates that some customers may have received fraudulent messages from the compromised account.
questions.question: What should the business consider doing?
options: Continue sending messages from the account
questions.feedback: Affected customers should be considered in the response so they can avoid further harm.

questions.story: The business wants to reduce the likelihood of a similar incident happening again.
questions.question: Which combination would provide stronger protection?
options: Security awareness and stronger account protection
questions.feedback: Security awareness and stronger account protection can reduce the likelihood and impact of similar incidents.

questions.story: The incident has been contained and investigated. The business now reviews what could have been done better.
questions.question: Why is a lessons-learned review useful?
options: It can identify weaknesses and improve future preparedness
It guarantees that attacks will never happen
It removes the need for security controls
questions.feedback: Lessons learned can help identify weaknesses and improve future prevention, detection and response.

questions.story: The complete simulated incident has now been reviewed from attack recognition through investigation and response.
questions.question: Which approach best demonstrates forensic readiness?
options: Having relevant evidence sources identified and procedures for preserving and investigating them
Waiting until an incident occurs before thinking about evidence
questions.feedback: Forensic readiness involves knowing what evidence may be available and having processes for preserving and investigating it.
